newsitem.title: THAILAND: Three Thai firms say not hit by forex losses.
newsitem.headline: Three Thai firms say not hit by forex losses.

text.p: The Cogeneration Plc, Banpu Plc and Siam Makro Plc said on Tuesday they were not affected by recent volatility in the foreign exchange market after the baht's fall on the dollar's surge.

They also detailed their U.S. dollar and Thai baht debt positions to clarify their finances in separate filings to the Thai stock exchange. The bourse was hit by talk on Tuesday morning that some listed firms may have been affected by the recent baht slide against the dollar, brokers said.
Coal miner Banpu denied local media reports that its profit and loss situation would be affected by the recent exchange rate volatility. Reports it had also borrowed $1 billion were untrue, it added.
Supermarket chain Siam Makro also denied media reports that it had borrowed $1 billion.

Power firm, The Cogeneration, said the company and its subsidiaries had debts denominated in dollars worth $229 million, which had been secured out of risk by exchanging in baht amounting to $168 million dollars since last October.
The firm conversion of its convertible debentures worth $100-200 million would not be due until February 2007.
Banpu also clarified that it had not taken any loans in German marks.
The company said its $80 million in convertible debentures, due in August 2004, had been 90 percent converted while another $100 million worth of debentures due in April 2003 were non-convertible.
Siam Makro said as of February 10 its total loans and interest in foreign currency amounted to $15.24 million and it had insured the whole amount from the risk of exchange rate fluctuation.
In addition, Siam Makro said its debts incurred from goods purchases and other transactions in foreign currencies amounted to $646,886, 122,068 sterling and 62,000 marks.
